scope: A claim is the statement with its stated hypotheses, sector and coefficient ring. IDs are stable; all local paths resolve from the project root. Replays may verify a named ingredient only. Inputs from other manuscripts are explicitly attributed. When present, continuation links to the exact next calculation.

statuses.proved: A proof or an exact certificate establishes the stated result in the indicated theory, sector and ring. The evidence field gives the warrant; a fresh numerical or symbolic replay is a separate attribute.
statuses.conditional: The implication is proved; a named physical identification or operator identity is still needed for the conclusion in the proposed theory.
statuses.literature-input: A result imported from the cited primary source; any local calculation checks the stated use of that input.
statuses.finite-evidence: A concrete observation in a bounded range or finite field; no rational or all-degree conclusion beyond the stated scope.
statuses.conjecture: A proposed positive pattern or identification; the available examples do not prove it.
statuses.open: A specified question still lacks a decisive calculation or proof. The record states the missing test.

claims.limits: The external theorem is perturbative. It supplies no instanton homotopy or physical coefficient.

claims.title: The exact homotopy identity does not force automatic contraction

claims.limits: This is a counterexample in linear algebra, not to the conditional secondary-pairing theorem or to a gauge theory.

claims.title: Massive bilinear Konishi identities and the zero-mass specialization
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(2) adjoint or one vectorlike flavor

claims.limits: Perturbative survival in the full stated jet complex. The physical instanton image is a separate local insertion problem.

claims.title: Magnetic rank exclusion and the Nc massive vacua
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, electric SU(Nc), magnetic SU(Nf−Nc)
claims.sector: Meson rank patches and isolated stationary vacua
claims.coefficient_ring: Holomorphic rank patches; invert the nonzero mass determinant only in the massive case
claims.hypotheses: Use the matched thresholds and all condensate sheets in §15. Distinguish the massless theory from the mass-deformed theory.
claims.statement: In the massless theory excess-rank magnetic stationary vacua are excluded, so rank⟨M⟩≤Nc. For invertible m, S^Nc=Λ^(3Nc−Nf)det m, ⟨M⟩=S m⁻¹ and W_vac=Nc S give Nc vacua.
claims.limits: Vacuum rank constraints are not a local operator differential; the massive meson values need not obey the massless vacuum rank bound.

claims.title: An ADS pole, saturation and the condensate sheets
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, Nf<Nc; explicit SU(2) decoupling
claims.sector: Effective scalar functions after eliminating massive fields
claims.coefficient_ring: Meson algebra localized at det M≠0; choose a condensate sheet only after solving the polynomial relation
claims.hypotheses: Use the source mass thresholds and eliminate only on the open set where the elimination equations can be solved.
claims.statement: S^(Nc−Nf) det M=Λ^(3Nc−Nf), W_eff=(Nc−Nf)S. The SU(2) one-flavor answer is Λ_L⁵/M, with Λ_L⁵=m₂Λ⁴; adding m₁M gives M²=Λ_L⁵/m₁. The contracted ideal on the patch is obtained by saturation.
claims.limits: A pole marks an elimination domain; clearing denominators cannot add M=0 as a solution. Different roots are different branches.

claims.title: Global effective Jacobian identity without inverting a meson
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(2), two-flavor constrained model with one mass
claims.sector: Constrained effective polynomial algebra and its ADS patch
claims.coefficient_ring: Global polynomial Jacobian quotient; formal scale versus fixed m₂Λ⁴≠0
claims.hypotheses: Keep the constrained fields, baryons and Lagrange multiplier when taking derivatives.
claims.statement: An explicit polynomial combination of all relevant F-equations equals m₂Λ⁴ globally. At fixed m₂Λ⁴≠0 the unit is exact throughout the constrained model. On the ADS patch Q(M̄²β)=conjugate(Λ_L⁵); before inverting that parameter this gives torsion.
claims.limits: An exact unit in this effective Koszul complex is not evidence for exactness in the full four-dimensional electric jet complex without a chain map.

claims.title: Quantum-modified moduli space versus s-confining equations
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(2), two and three flavors
claims.sector: Antisymmetric meson V and its exact low-energy scalar relations
claims.coefficient_ring: Complex scalar algebra, fixed nonzero dynamical scale
claims.hypotheses: Use the source Pfaffian ordering; the two flavor counts are different theories.
claims.statement: At Nf=2, Pf V=Λ⁴ is a smooth five-dimensional vacuum variety. At Nf=3, W=−Pf V/Λ³ imposes rank V≤2; all 15 mesons are massless at the origin.
claims.limits: Deforming a scalar constraint and enforcing the classical composite rank are different effects; neither example supplies a microscopic jet primitive here.

claims.title: Symplectic Pfaffian mass descent
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SP(2) in the Intriligator–Pouliot rank convention
claims.sector: Confining superpotential, quantum constraint and ADS daughter
claims.coefficient_ring: Source holomorphic scales; invert the remaining Pfaffian only on the ADS patch
claims.hypotheses: The fundamental of SP(Nc) has complex dimension 2Nc; follow the source mass thresholds.
claims.statement: At Nf=4 the superpotential is −Pf M/(2Λ_(2,4)^5); at Nf=3 the constraint is Pf M=2Λ_(2,3)^6; at Nf=2 the superpotential is 2Λ_(2,2)^7/Pf M.
claims.limits: The numerical factors are tied to the SP source normalization. These are low-energy relations, not new microscopic instanton amplitudes.

claims.title: Orthogonal determinant coefficient and flat-branch cancellation
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SO(Nc), Nf=Nc−1
claims.sector: Effective instanton and gaugino-condensate contributions
claims.coefficient_ring: Fixed nonzero source scales; keep both condensate signs
claims.hypotheses: Use the Intriligator–Seiberg scale matching, the stated group and the low-rank convention.
claims.statement: W_inst=−det M/(64Λ^(2Nc−5)), W_cond=ε det M/(64Λ^(2Nc−5)), ε=±1. The ε=+1 branch has exact cancellation; retaining only the instanton term would delete this flat branch.
claims.limits: Branches, low-rank global forms and line operators have to be tracked; no universal lift across orthogonal dualities is inferred.

claims.title: Higher fermionic F-terms and their mass descent
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(2), four flavors and its mass descendants
claims.sector: Effective interaction class over the regular Higgs branch
claims.coefficient_ring: Regular global sections satisfying the physical admissibility conditions
claims.hypotheses: Use the Beasley–Witten zero-mode measure and the global constraints on admissible primitives.
claims.statement: Two universal and six matter zero modes produce an eight-fermion interaction. Its radial integral equals 360(g²/(4π²|v|²))⁷. Local primitives do not glue to an admissible global one; successive masses descend to the lower-flavor interactions.
claims.limits: This is not an ordinary scalar superpotential. The absolute coefficient and a four-dimensional scalar jet differential are not determined by the radial integral.

claims.title: Monopole torsion on a finite circle
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(Nc), Nf=Nc on a circle
claims.sector: Three-dimensional scalar algebra extended by the monopole disorder operator Y
claims.coefficient_ring: Formal circle parameter η, or specified fixed η≠0
claims.hypotheses: Use W=Y(B B̃−det M+η) in the order and sign of §19; treat Y as a disorder coordinate of this effective theory.
claims.statement: The F-equations imply η[Y]=0. Y is detected at η=0. At fixed nonzero η its explicit odd primitive gives [Y]=0 and the quotient is C[M,B,B̃]/(det M−B B̃−η).
claims.limits: The symbolic replay checks the Euler identity at Nc=2,3; the derivative proof is general. Y is not a four-dimensional polynomial jet operator.

claims.title: Benchmarks: monopole removal, exact unit, and quantum ring deformation
claims.theory: 3d N=2 Aharony duality; 2d (0,2) and (2,2) sigma models
claims.sector: Monopole disorder classes, a chiral algebra, and a twisted chiral ring, respectively
claims.coefficient_ring: Use each source ring; for the (0,2) model distinguish formal weight and fixed nonzero weight
claims.hypotheses: Elementary singlet differentiation in the magnetic theory; minimal (0,2) CP¹ without left movers; (2,2) CP^(N−1) mirror conventions.
claims.statement: Aharony singlet F-equations remove the two magnetic monopoles. In minimal (0,2) CP¹ the unit becomes exact at fixed nonzero instanton weight. For (2,2) CP^(N−1), σ^N=Λ^N instead gives N vacua.
claims.limits: These are mechanisms in different operator spaces and spacetime dimensions; do not infer four-dimensional class removal from the analogy.

claims.title: The cubic adjoint trace has exact classical nilpotency index three
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(5), four flavors and a cubic adjoint
claims.sector: Adjoint trace quotient inside the full classical invariant F-term algebra
claims.coefficient_ring: C, polynomial gauge invariants with their ideal (not its radical)
claims.hypotheses: Keep the traceless adjoint and its full matrix F-equation; work at zero quadratic adjoint deformation.
claims.statement: The trace subalgebra for u=Tr X² is C[u]/(u³): u³=0 while u²≠0. The determinant/Cayley–Hamilton calculation and nonreduced detector retain the nilpotent.
claims.limits: A nilpotent cannot be detected solely by its values on ordinary complex vacua.

claims.title: The nonzero SU(5) trace square survives the perturbative Ward complex
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(5), four flavors and a cubic adjoint
claims.sector: Pure scalar, zero derivative order, tested against the full specified Ward kernels
claims.coefficient_ring: C[[hbar]], nonnegative loop powers
claims.hypotheses: The stated anomaly-free source complex, gauge generators, matter interaction and graph rules; use the scalar-extraction map on all allowed primitives.
claims.statement: The square of Tr X² (in the source conjugate representative) is closed and nonexact. No nonzero power of hbar annihilates its class in the specified formal complex.
claims.limits: The perturbative detector does not impose the stronger square-zero relation in the exact quantum chiral ring.

claims.title: Does the magnetic trace square vanish with dynamical mesons?
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, SU(5), four flavors and a cubic adjoint; magnetic SU(3)
claims.sector: Full renormalized quantum scalar operator ring
claims.coefficient_ring: Fixed source couplings at zero quadratic deformation; include meson operators
claims.hypotheses: Kutasov–Schwimmer–Seiberg obtain the stronger trace prediction at the mesonic origin. Promote the operator map, singlet equations and characteristic relation to a common scheme only after deriving them.
claims.statement: The magnetic trace presentation predicts (Tr X²)²=0 at the mesonic origin. A relation with dynamical mesons in the full electric ring, and a microscopic instanton primitive for that class, remain unproved.
claims.limits: The replay checks the deformed trace and branch calculations only. Matching ordinary vacua cannot settle a nilpotent operator identity.

claims.title: Two-adjoint D-even and E7 truncations are not established lift certificates
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD with two adjoints
claims.sector: Proposed quantum truncation of the scalar chiral ring
claims.coefficient_ring: As in the named ADE gauge theories; no project operator complex or normalization assumed
claims.hypotheses: Distinguish an assumed magnetic spectrum from a demonstrated electric operator identity; account for nilpotent flat directions.
claims.statement: Intriligator–Nardoni discuss counterevidence to proposed D-even and E7 truncations. Bryan–Rajaraman–Shirman separately report a failure of the proposed D_(k+2) duality on nilpotent directions. Neither supplies a positive microscopic instanton lift here.
claims.limits: The D-series test does not establish a corresponding E7 failure. No local certificate or spectrum calculation for these theories is included.

claims.title: Seiberg–Witten periods, singular curves and mass-induced condensation
claims.theory: 4d N=2 SU(2) and SU(3) SQCD
claims.sector: Coulomb geometry, periods, prepotential and mass-selected vacua
claims.coefficient_ring: Pure SU(2) strong scale one for period coefficients; restored scale and magnetic frame for the condensate
claims.hypotheses: Fix the source curve and electric/magnetic cycles. The monopole condensate additionally needs the adjoint mass deformation.
claims.statement: For pure SU(2), F1=1/(8πi), F2=5/(256πi). At adjoint mass m the vacua have u=±Λ² and W=±mΛ², with M M̃=i√2 mΛ in the specified monopole frame. §21 includes flavor-dependent discriminants and the SU(3), Nf=6 Argyres–Seiberg curve.
claims.limits: These are exact examples of geometry and vacuum data, not a computed nonscalar microscopic supercharge differential.

claims.title: Exact diagonal vacua detect every nonzero pure-scalar class
claims.theory: 4d N=4 SYM, SU(N)
claims.sector: Gauge-invariant pure-scalar quotient of three commuting traceless matrices
claims.coefficient_ring: Complex scalar invariants in characteristic zero
claims.hypotheses: Use the reduced invariant quotient (Vaccarino), survival of the exact diagonal vacua, and vanishing of exact operator insertions in supersymmetric vacua.
claims.statement: A nonzero invariant scalar is nonzero on a simultaneous diagonal vacuum. Its exact expectation value rules out its becoming Q-exact by an instanton.
claims.limits: The reduced invariant quotient is not the unreduced commuting scheme. No claim for operators with derivatives, fermions or invisible nilpotents in unrelated theories.

claims.title: One-loop class pairing versus the long Konishi instanton correction
claims.theory: 4d N=4 SYM, SO(7)/USp(6) and SU(N)
claims.sector: Specified tree classes in the dual pair; a distinct long-multiplet anomalous dimension
claims.coefficient_ring: First perturbative order, and one-instanton plus anti-instanton sector in the cited SU(N) convention
claims.hypotheses: Use the stated generalized Konishi differential for the dual pair and the Alday–Korchemsky normalization for the separate long-operator calculation.
claims.statement: The known SO(7)/USp(6) pairing is perturbative. In SU(N) the long Konishi anomalous dimension has a nonzero instanton Fourier coefficient; in SU(2) the multiplier of (g²/(4π²))²(exp(2πiτ)+exp(−2πi conjugate τ)) is −9/5.
claims.limits: Neither observed effect is a microscopic instanton removal of a class surviving all perturbative orders.

claims.title: Positivity restricts a proposed leading instanton energy matrix
claims.theory: 4d N=4 SYM
claims.sector: Effective energy on a finite-dimensional space of perturbative survivors
claims.coefficient_ring: Real vacuum angle θ and positive weak-coupling weight; Hermitian inner product
claims.hypotheses: Use a positive BPS Hamiltonian at every θ, the uniform leading expansion and the controlled projection stated in §22.
claims.statement: A positive leading matrix with zero angular mean is identically zero. This excludes an energy shift built solely of nonzero Fourier modes at that order; a first-instanton supercharge coefficient d can give a neutral positive term {d,d†}.
claims.limits: The hypotheses do not prove the absence of nonscalar instanton pairings; the quadratic, neutral energy term is compatible with positivity.

claims.title: A microscopic instanton image on a nonscalar perturbative survivor
claims.theory: 4d N=4 SYM
claims.sector: One-supercharge cohomology with fermions or derivatives
claims.coefficient_ring: Instanton filtration after perturbative cohomology
claims.hypotheses: Identify an actual all-perturbative survivor, the charge-matched target and all trivial images in that sector.
claims.statement: No such nonzero microscopic instanton matrix element is certified in this collection.
claims.limits: Zero-mode counting without the full insertions, long-operator correlators, and a classical duality mismatch are not sufficient tests. The total-translation subspace of one-scalar half-BPS primaries is excluded by the exact two-point detector.

claims.title: Full magnetic determinant torsion ideal
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, electric Nf=Nc+2 with one mass, magnetic SU(2) Higgs patch
claims.sector: All scalar polynomial degrees of the light effective F-term quotient
claims.coefficient_ring: C[magnetic weight], or its parameter-adic completion; fixed nonzero μ,m
claims.hypotheses: Use the light magnetic quarks as regular coordinates, the full cofactor F-equations, and independent formal instanton weight.
claims.statement: The localization kernel is det(M̂)·C[M̂]. The annihilator of its generator is the weight and all light quark and antiquark entries. Every scalar target in this ideal is on the first instanton page.
claims.limits: Proof covers the full specified scalar family. Independent eliminations are for matrix sizes two and three. A microscopic action requires the local Ward comparison.

claims.title: Necessary residue and obstruction to mass-regular microscopic matching
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, four-flavor magnetic SU(2)
claims.sector: Tree-loop coefficient of a putative one-instanton local action on the light-row current
claims.coefficient_ring: Parameter-linear prescription regular in hbar; fixed nonzero μ,g and variable mass
claims.hypotheses: Assume nilpotency through first instanton order, nonnegative loop powers also for perturbative boundary comparisons, and the determinant projection claimed on the punctured mass family.
claims.statement: On the explicit F-flat evaluation the proposed matching requires ev_m(DA)=3 det(conjugate M̂)/(conjugate μ^4 conjugate m) with the weight stripped. A mass-regular polynomial DA cannot have this value.
claims.limits: A necessary test on one scalar projection. It leaves the physical amplitude on the punctured Higgs patch open, and uses a specified loop filtration.

claims.title: Different complete torsion ideals for two presentations of the same confined theory
claims.theory: 4d N=1 SQCD, completely broken magnetic SP(1); electric SP(1)=SU(2) comparison at six light meson flavors
claims.sector: Effective scalar F-terms in regular light coordinates of each presentation
claims.coefficient_ring: Separate formal magnetic weights; fixed nonzero masses and matching scales; fixed common nonzero electric scale for the fiber comparison
claims.hypotheses: Use the Intriligator–Pouliot Pfaffian potential, then compare the six-index Pfaffian in interleaved flavor order with Seiberg's magnetic quark coordinates.
claims.statement: The complete symplectic scalar kernel is the ideal of submaximal Pfaffians modulo the weight times that ideal. At six flavors it has 15 quadratic generators. The SU presentation has one cubic determinant generator; the zero-weight fibers have dimensions 15 and 9. Their generic superpotentials agree after baryon rescaling.
claims.limits: The nonzero-weight identification uses a square root after choosing a fixed fiber or adjoining the root. The two choices of regular fields define different formal families.

claims.title: All effective Pfaffian jet torsion and the first 105 fermionic targets
claims.theory: 4d holomorphic effective meson theory obtained on the broken SP(1) magnetic branch
claims.sector: Full polynomial scalar/odd jet complex of the ungauged Pfaffian model; explicit zero-derivative target counts
claims.coefficient_ring: Nonnegative powers of the magnetic weight with other matching coefficients fixed and invertible
claims.hypotheses: Use the retained Pfaffian interaction and ordinary polynomial jets. Its vertices contain only scalar letters.
claims.statement: All parameter torsion is the constant-coefficient image of the weight-stripped Koszul operation and has exponent one. At six flavor slots the target with two scalar letters and p−1 odd partners has rank binomial(15,p) for 1≤p≤15, including 105 in the first fermionic sector.
claims.limits: The fermionic and higher-jet claims refer to the specified holomorphic effective model. Matching these local representatives to microscopic operators or additional higher interactions is a distinct calculation.

claims.title: All positive-degree monopole torsion and the multiplier criterion
claims.theory: Compactified SU(Nc) SQCD with Nf=Nc and the algebraic family W=Y(F+η)
claims.sector: Scalar F-terms at all Y degrees
claims.coefficient_ring: Polynomial parameter or parameter-adic completion; a stated localization of the scalar domain is allowed
claims.hypotheses: F is nonzero in the scalar domain, Y is an independent multiplier. For the circle use F=B B̃−det M in the source normalization.
claims.statement: At Y-degree j≥1 the parameter acts by −F on the Jacobian algebra of F. For the circle the entire torsion is (Y), with coefficients C[M] modulo all (Nc−1)-minors, supported at zero baryons and rank at most Nc−2.
claims.limits: Circle compactification supplies a three-dimensional disorder operator and a known finite-circle term. The general multiplier statement concerns the given effective scalar algebra.

claims.title: A linear superpotential deformation with a genuine second-page scalar target
claims.theory: Local polynomial multiplier model W=Y(x^5+y^5+x^3y^3+η)
claims.sector: Every positive Y-degree, localized at x=y=0
claims.coefficient_ring: C[x,y] localized at the origin with formal η, or the corresponding completion
claims.hypotheses: The local polynomial 25−9xy is a unit at the chosen point.
claims.statement: Multiplication by F on the 16-dimensional local Jacobian algebra has rank one and square zero. Each positive Y-degree has fourteen length-one blocks and one length-two block. η[Y^j]≠0 and η²[Y^j]=0 with an explicit local odd primitive.
claims.limits: This is an exact algebraic superpotential example. No gauge-instanton origin of its tunable parameter is assumed.

claims.title: Complete ghost-number-two sector and two protected bulk derivative towers
claims.theory: 4d pure N=2 Yang–Mills, complex simple gauge algebra
claims.sector: Relative holomorphic-topological basic jet complex; all spins
claims.coefficient_ring: Characteristic zero with a complete formal deformation of neutral spin and ghost grading
claims.hypotheses: Start with Khan's relative tree complex. The deformed differential preserves spin, raises ghost number by one, and commutes with holomorphic translation on filtered cohomology; no extra sectors in the initial page.
claims.statement: Ghost-number-two cohomology is one-dimensional at each spin s≥2 and generated by derivatives of the mixed invariant. Its tower and the pure-b invariant cubic tower admit neither incoming nor outgoing differentials, at every order. The ∂X→Y pairing is excluded in this bulk setting.
claims.limits: The proof uses the specified simple-algebra bulk complex and Ward identity. The replay tests SU(2) through spin 16; the mode recurrence proves every spin. Defect sectors and other twists have other hypotheses.

claims.title: Conditional collapse if the two-generator bulk presentation is complete
claims.theory: 4d pure N=2 SU(2), Khan's holomorphic-topological algebra A
claims.sector: All operators in the proposed differential supercommutative algebra
claims.coefficient_ring: One formal parameter of spin and ghost number zero
claims.hypotheses: Identify the entire perturbative algebra, product and translation with Khan's A, and use a multiplicative filtered bulk differential compatible with translation.
claims.statement: Every product derivation of spin zero and ghost number one commuting with translation vanishes on A. Hence under the identification all induced instanton differentials vanish. The proposed algebraic map sends ∂X to the nonzero Y.
claims.limits: Full identification with A is conjectural in the cited source. The separate protection of the two towers uses the complete bilinear calculation without this identification.

claims.title: Saturation and finite-sector invariant factors
claims.theory: Scalar effective presentations and finite free operator complexes
claims.sector: Scalar quotients, or a fixed outgoing kernel and its incoming map
claims.coefficient_ring: A polynomial weight for saturation; a single discrete valuation ring C[[η]] for Smith form
claims.hypotheses: Supply the actual differential, choose the regular operators and a flat finite free chain sector in the matrix calculation.
claims.statement: For scalar equations I the localization kernel is (I:η^∞)/I. In the finite free case the successive minimum valuations of the nonzero minors determine all exponents of incoming torsion pairs and their first nonzero pages.
claims.limits: These are standard algebraic tools applied to the indicated operator data. A differential cannot be reconstructed from a vacuum count or an unspecified matrix.

claims.title: Exact dimension of the translated one-scalar half-BPS subspace
claims.theory: Unitary four-dimensional N=4 SU(N) SYM in flat-space radial quantization
claims.sector: Total holomorphic derivatives of one-complex-scalar half-BPS primaries of degree p≥2
claims.coefficient_ring: Physical unitary coupling with positive radial inner product
claims.hypotheses: Use the exact half-BPS primaries, traceless SU(N) scalar invariant ring, two holomorphic translations, and the superconformal bound in the Chang–Yin normalization.
claims.statement: At derivative order k the protected subspace has dimension (k+1) times the coefficient of t^p in the product of (1−t^j)⁻¹ over j=2,…,N. Its exact two-point derivative polynomials distinguish every component.
claims.limits: A consequence of half-BPS representation theory and unitary conformal symmetry. The count is for total translation descendants, not the multiplicity of every spinful primary or independently distributed jet.

claims.title: A microscopic two-parameter base-change kernel and its secondary differential
claims.theory: 4d N=1 magnetic SU(2) with four flavors and variable mass for the fourth pair
claims.sector: Relative polynomial Ward jets over the joint mass and loop family
claims.coefficient_ring: C[[conjugate m,hbar]], fixed nonzero g,μ
claims.hypotheses: Use the polynomial current, the two source-normalized primitive equations for the Cartan ghost trace, independent parameters, and the complete three-letter source obstruction.
claims.statement: The quadratic ghost trace has scalar annihilator (conjugate m,hbar). The polynomial incoming current has zero scalar annihilator. Its class is nonzero in cohomology modulo the maximal ideal yet becomes a boundary in the jointly specialized complex. The two-generator Koszul resolution has an explicit nonzero second differential onto its reduction up to the coefficient of Theorem 16.5.
claims.limits: This nonzero second differential concerns joint specialization of microscopic perturbative cohomology. Its order is the degree of the parameter resolution, not an instanton number.
